answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a refundable bond before joining a shared registry, an atlas of verified identities. Newcomers start with only a kernel of limited privileges and earn broader access by completing verifiable work over time. An attacker spawning thousands of clones gains nothing: each fake identity must post its own bond and grind through the same slow reef of costly, auditable tasks, so forgery scales linearly in cost while honest agents, once vetted, trade freely.
